alt: A living room in late-afternoon sun with all four EARF pieces in Poison: a pair of Tropos speakers reading as bright green glass, the woofers and their insides showing, with deep green stepped horns, their covers off, each on a stepped plinth, either side of a low oak credenza with a Mantle record player whose dark deck floats on steel posts over a smoked base; a green Core lamp on a side table at the left; a deep green Hemisphere pendant over a cognac leather chair at the right; a plain plaster wall behind
notes: Each piece takes its name from the Earth. Tropos is Greek for a turn; the troposphere, the layer of air we live in, is named for it. Core, Mantle and Hemisphere are the planet’s own parts. Here all four share one room, in Poison, one of the eight colors. Tropos is in the line’s final colors: Poison poured a step lighter, over a white lining, so the cabinet reads as green glass. It is a render, not a photograph: Tropos with its stepped horn and its cover off, on its lit plinth; Core cordless; Mantle as Strata Float, its deck floating on steel posts over a smoked base; Hemisphere with its color outside. A version of the same room at dusk, with the lights on, exists.

header.title: Four pieces, named for the Earth.
